verdict.rationale: Both changes make config loading strict in nearly the same way: they collect every problem, reject unknown keys, fail on a missing file, and print the problems and exit from Main. B has stronger edge-case tests (blank token, empty optional value, overflowing timeout, boundary values accepted, case-insensitive booleans, http accepted). Its report is precise, with a correct test count. A also adds an unrequested rule rejecting a zero timeout, and its report miscounts the new tests.
a_issues: Rejects request.timeout=0s, which the README and task do not require (a small scope expansion, though it is disclosed)
Report says 10 new tests, but the diff adds 11
No tests confirm that valid boundary values (worker.threads=1, retry.max-attempts=0, http URL, TRUE) are still accepted
b_issues: ConfigLoader becomes a stateful instance with a mutable problems list; this is a little more structure than needed
No test checks that the api.token value stays out of error messages, even though the report claims it does
The missing-file message reuses the generic 'Cannot read' text with the exception's toString instead of a clear 'not found' message

verdict.rationale: The two changes are nearly equivalent: both collect every problem, reject unknown keys, bad values, a missing file and a bad URL, and exit with a clear message. A sticks more closely to the documented rules and its tests cover boundaries in both directions (the minimum accepted, minus one rejected). Its report is accurate. B quietly adds a new rule rejecting a zero timeout, adds a problems-list API to the exception, and its report misstates the old upstream.url behavior and the number of new tests.
a_issues: Exit code 2 is less conventional than EX_CONFIG (78) for configuration errors
No explicit test that the api.token value stays out of error messages
b_issues: Rejects request.timeout=0s, a new rule not in the README; this goes beyond the task
Adds a problems list and accessor to ConfigException that only tests use
Report says a missing upstream.url crashed with a NullPointerException, but the old code caught it and returned null
Report says 10 new tests; the diff adds 11
Tests don't check that boundary values (minimum allowed) are still accepted
